title: Particles: へ/に, から & まで
description: Going places with へ and に, starting points with から, and end points with まで (vs. までに).

points.title: に / へ: to (destination)
points.summary: With movement verbs (行く, 来る, 帰る), both に and へ mark the destination. へ stresses direction and can take の.
points.body:
With **行く・来る・帰る・戻る** and similar movement verbs, both particles work:
- 日本**に**行きます: に points at the **arrival point**.
- 日本**へ**行きます: へ (pronounced え) stresses the **direction**.

In everyday speech they are mostly interchangeable. The differences that matter:
- **Only に** can mark non-movement targets: 友達に会う, バスに乗る, 先生に聞く. へ can't replace these.
- **Only へ** can be followed by の to modify a noun: 母**への**手紙 (a letter to my mother). に can't: 母にの手紙 ✗.
- **Only に** is used for purpose: 買い物に行く.

When in doubt with movement verbs, に is always safe.
examples: {来年|らいねん}、{日本|にほん}へ{行|い}きます。
I'm going to Japan next year.
{何時|なんじ}に{家|うち}に{帰|かえ}りますか。
What time are you going home?
これは{先生|せんせい}への{プレゼント|ぷれぜんと}です。
This is a present for the teacher.

points.title: から (2): from
points.summary: Noun + から marks a starting point in place or time, or a source (who something comes from).
points.body:
から marks **where something starts**:
- **Place**: 駅から歩きます (walk from the station).
- **Time**: 9時から始まります (it starts at/from 9).
- **Source / sender**: 母から手紙が来ました (a letter came from my mother), 友達からもらいました (I got it from a friend).

It very often pairs with まで: **AからBまで** = 'from A to/until B'.

Don't confuse it with **から (1) = because**, which follows a full clause (高いから), while 'from' follows a noun (東京から). And with the て-form, **てから** means 'after doing'.
examples: {授業|じゅぎょう}は9{時|じ}から{始|はじ}まります。
{国|くに}の{母|はは}から{荷物|にもつ}が{届|とど}きました。
A package arrived from my mother back home.
{東京|とうきょう}から{大阪|おおさか}まで{新幹線|しんかんせん}で{行|い}きます。
I'll go from Tokyo to Osaka by Shinkansen.

points.title: まで: until, to, as far as
points.summary: まで marks an end point in place or time. Something continues up to that point. Compare までに = 'by (a deadline)'.
points.body:
まで marks **where or when something ends**:
- **Place**: 駅まで歩きます (walk as far as the station).
- **Time**: 5時まで働きます (work until 5).

The action **continues the whole way** up to that point.

**まで vs までに** (a classic trap):
- **まで** goes with a continuing action or state: 5時**まで**待ちます (I'll keep waiting until 5).
- **までに** marks a deadline for a one-time action: 5時**までに**来てください (come **by** 5).

With verbs, use the dictionary form: 母が帰るまで待ちます (I'll wait until mother comes home).

まで can also mean 'even': 子供まで知っています (even children know). This use is less common at N5.
examples: {家|いえ}から{駅|えき}まで{歩|ある}きます。
I walk from home to the station.
9{時|じ}から5{時|じ}まで{働|はたら}きます。
{金曜日|きんようび}までにレポートを{出|だ}してください。
Please hand in the report by Friday.

questions.prompt: {来月|らいげつ}、{国|くに}（　）{帰|かえ}ります。
questions.explanation: With 帰る, the destination takes **へ** (or に).
notes: を with movement verbs marks a route you pass through, not a destination.
が would make the country the subject that goes home.
で marks the place of an action. 国で帰ります doesn't make sense.
questions.translation: I'm going back to my home country next month.

questions.prompt: これは{母|はは}（　）の{手紙|てがみ}です。
questions.explanation: Only **へ** can combine with の to modify a noun: 母への手紙 = 'a letter to my mother'.
notes: がの isn't a valid combination.
にの is impossible. に can't be followed by の.
をの isn't a valid combination.
questions.translation: This is a letter to my mother.

questions.prompt: {駅|えき}で{友達|ともだち}（　）{会|あ}いました。
questions.explanation: 会う marks the person you meet with **に** (or と). へ only works for direction with movement verbs.
notes: 友達を会う is a very common mistake. 会う takes に.
で would mean 'by means of a friend'. The place is already 駅で.
へ is only for direction with movement verbs. You can't use it with 会う.
questions.translation: I met a friend at the station.

questions.prompt: デパートへ{買|か}い{物|もの}（　）{行|い}きます。
questions.explanation: The purpose of going takes **に**: 買い物に行く. へ can't mark purpose.
notes: で marks a place or means of an action.
へ marks direction (デパートへ already does). It can't mark a purpose.
買い物をします is fine, but 買い物を行きます isn't.
questions.translation: I'm going to the department store to go shopping.

questions.prompt: {国|くに}の{友達|ともだち}（　）メールが{来|き}ました。
questions.explanation: The sender or source takes **から**.
notes: を would make the friend an object.
まで marks an end point. The email didn't go 'as far as' the friend.
で would mean 'by means of a friend'.
questions.translation: An email came from my friend back home.

questions.prompt: {銀行|ぎんこう}は{何時|なんじ}（　）ですか。—9{時|じ}からです。
questions.explanation: The answer 9時からです tells you the question is about the opening time: **から**.
notes: 何時にですか isn't natural with です here.
何時までですか asks about the closing time. The answer would then be 〜までです.
何時でですか isn't a form.
questions.translation: From what time is the bank open? — From 9.

questions.prompt: この{本|ほん}は{図書館|としょかん}（　）{借|か}りました。
questions.explanation: The source you borrow from takes **から**.
notes: まで means 'as far as', which doesn't fit borrowing.
へ marks a direction toward something.
With 借りる, に marks the person you borrow from (友達に借りる). For an institution like a library, から is natural.
questions.translation: I borrowed this book from the library.

questions.prompt: {家|いえ}から{駅|えき}（　）{歩|ある}いて{行|い}きます。
notes: 駅で歩く would be 'walk (around) inside the station'.
から already marks the start (家から). The station is the end point.
までに means 'by (a deadline)' and is used for time, not as the end point of a route.
questions.translation: I walk from my house to the station.

questions.prompt: 9{時|じ}から5{時|じ}（　）{働|はたら}きます。
questions.explanation: Working continues up to 5, so it's **まで** ('until').
notes: を doesn't mark time here.
5時に働きます would mean 'work at 5 o'clock', and it clashes with 9時から.
までに means 'by (a deadline)', for a one-time action. Working is continuous, so it needs まで.

questions.prompt: {金曜日|きんようび}（　）{宿題|しゅくだい}を{出|だ}してください。
questions.explanation: Handing something in is a one-time action with a deadline, so it takes **までに** ('by Friday').
notes: で doesn't mark a deadline.
まで would mean 'keep handing it in until Friday', a continuing action.
から means 'from Friday', not a deadline.
questions.translation: Please hand in your homework by Friday.

questions.prompt: {雨|あめ}がやむ（　）、ここで{待|ま}ちましょう。
questions.explanation: We keep waiting up to the point the rain stops, so it's **まで** after the dictionary form.
notes: ので ('because it stops') doesn't fit.
から would mean 'after/because the rain stops, let's wait', which is illogical.
までに is a deadline for a single action. Waiting is continuous.
questions.translation: Let's wait here until the rain stops.

questions.prompt: {仕事|しごと}は{何時|なんじ}（　）{何時|なんじ}までですか。
questions.explanation: **AからBまで** = from A to B.
notes: まで is already used for the end point.
何時に何時まで isn't the range pattern.
何時で何時まで isn't grammatical.
questions.translation: What time to what time is your work?

questions.prompt: {駅|えき}（　）{迎|むか}えに{来|き}てください。
questions.explanation: **まで** marks 'as far as' a place.
notes: までに is a time deadline, not a place.
駅から迎えに来て = 'come from the station to pick me up' — wrong direction.
駅で迎えに来て isn't natural; you'd say 駅まで / 駅に.
questions.translation: Please come to pick me up at the station.
